candidates.summary: The whole-row copy (94 bytes a pass, 13.75 cycles a byte) made self-modifying: four LDA abs,Y / STA abs,Y sites whose operands are set once a whole row from d_ptr and s_ptr (76 cycles, 16 stores), so each byte costs 4+5+2 instead of 5+6+2: 2 cycles a byte against 76 a row. The part path (line8) and its pointers are untouched; d_ptr/s_ptr are still stored. Alternative to the second candidate (the unroll by 8), which it beats; they overlap.
candidates.equivalence: Same bytes copied in the same order (Y from the row's top byte down to 0, one DEY after each), same loop (BPL sdw_l1 on N after the fourth DEY, so the row's 8k bytes need the same multiple of 4 as before), same exits: BMI next_row always taken (Y=&FF..), A the last byte loaded, X untouched (next_row reloads it from sky_q), d_ptr/s_ptr unchanged in zero page. LDA abs,Y and STA abs,Y compute the same 16-bit address as the (zp),Y forms (low + Y, carry into the high byte, wrap at &FFFF); the page-cross +1 on the load is the same condition. The operands are set before the loop on every whole row, from the pointers as sky_row left them (A and Y are not used between: Z set, Y the top byte is kept). Part rows (BNE part) jump over the whole block; they never run the patched sites. The patches write the RAM the code runs from (ACCCON X: shadow's copy of &30xx when drawing the shadow screen, as the existing STA cell+1 does), and render_reset copies the whole of &3000-&3FFF main to shadow, so both copies carry the sites. No interrupt runs or reads these bytes. Built and run: tools/passlock.mjs plain build against the current one, 2,500 passes seed 1 with --screen: state identical, 0 screen bytes differing.
candidates.relies_on: Whole rows: Y+1 is a multiple of 8 (sky_geom's ry = 8*(d2-d1)+7 or, past &7FFF, 0 - rl - 8 with rl a multiple of 8), as before; the window's own BNE part / BMI next_row ranges (part now 88 bytes away: assembles, +162 would not; BMI next_row still 66). Page crossings: the loop (sdw_l1 &3111 to BPL at &312D, next PC &312F) stays inside page &31, the old loop in page &30; the 64 bytes added move everything after the window up 64: sky_zero (&313E -> &317E, loops all inside page &31), the per-screen variables (no base ending &FF, indexed by 0/1 or up to 9 without crossing) and sky_img0 (&317F -> &31BF), so helicopter 0's image blocks fall differently across the &3200/&3300 page boundaries (helicopter 1's, at &3E40, does not move). Measured on the plain build, pcprof 1500 passes seed 1: render 23432 -> 23284 cycles a pass (-148), and with SKIP 16 or 48 added before line8 (image at &31CF, &31EF) 23287 and 23293, so not an alignment accident. Uses 64 of the 193 free bytes at the end of the main block (unused_3400_original SKIP; gameplay builds have 13 more).

candidates.summary: Alternative to the first candidate (overlaps it; the safe one, no self-modification): the whole-row loop unrolled to eight bytes, halving the BPLs. Y+1 is always a multiple of 8 on a whole row (sky_geom), so the loop ends with Y = -1 as before.
candidates.equivalence: Identical copy sequence (LDA (d_ptr),Y / STA (s_ptr),Y / DEY, Y descending) and exit (BPL falls to BMI next_row with Y=&FF, N set, A the last byte). Y+1 = 8 * (columns) on every whole row: sky_geom sets ry = 8*(d2-d1) and rt = 7, so Y = 8*(d2-d1)+7, or, for the part of a row past &7FFF, ry = 0 - rl - 8 and 7 | ry with rl a multiple of 8 (a cell address), so the eight-byte loop never needs the half-iteration the four-byte one allowed. Registers, flags and zero page as before.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: the loop is now 42 bytes from &30D9, so the BPL (at &3101, next PC &3103) crosses into page &31 and each taken branch costs 4 not 3 (about 1 in 8 bytes: still 2 cycles saved per 8 bytes against 4 before); the 20 bytes added also move sky_zero, the variables and sky_img0 (&317F -> &3193). Measured plain build, pcprof 1500 passes: render 23432 -> 23389 (-43). 20 of 193 free bytes at the end of the main block.
